body:
Good Wednesday morning, Bakersfield. Today is Veterans Day, and the city's parade steps off downtown this morning — the marquee event on a warm, hazy holiday. Expect a high near 81 under mostly sunny skies, with a Lake Wind Advisory running through Saturday morning and air quality sitting in the moderate range. If you're headed to the route, sunscreen and a light jacket for the early hours both make sense.

## The Kern Overnight

It was a busy night for Kern County dispatchers, who logged 27 incidents between 7:04 p.m. and 6:42 a.m. Fires accounted for the largest share — 12 in all — with five medical or overdose calls, three reports of suspicious activity, two welfare and disturbance calls, and one commercial alarm.

The evening opened with a structure fire reported just after 7 p.m., followed within the half hour by a vehicle fire and a separate fire call. Around 8:15 p.m. crews were sent to a vehicle-versus-pedestrian incident, and a commercial fire alarm came in a few minutes later, alongside an outside fire. A fire near Truxtun Avenue was logged at 9:12 p.m., and another fire call came in just after 10 p.m. An officer assist and a probation check rounded out the late-evening entries.

Overnight, dispatchers handled medical aid calls at 12:16 a.m., 3:34 a.m., and 5:53 a.m., and three suspicious-person reports spread between 10:59 p.m. and 1:19 a.m. A welfare call near Jefferson Street came in at 1:58 a.m. Fire crews were dispatched again at 2:56 a.m., to a grass fire at 3:09 a.m., and to another fire at 3:54 a.m. A burglary was reported at 5:07 a.m., and the log closed with an outside fire near Golden State Avenue at 6:15 a.m. and a vehicle fire at 6:42 a.m.

A reminder that these entries come from preliminary dispatch reports and are generalized to protect privacy; details stand until an official source confirms them.

## Today's weather

It's 63 degrees at Meadows Field as of this morning, on the way to a high near 81 and a low around 55 tonight — a genuinely warm November day. The National Weather Service in Hanford has issued a Lake Wind Advisory that took effect at 9:33 a.m. and runs through 10 a.m. Saturday, so boaters and anyone working outside should plan for gusty conditions over the next few days. Air quality is 81, which registers as moderate; those with sensitivities may want to keep an eye on it as the day warms. No active fires were reported in the region.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield's Veterans Day Parade returns today**, with the annual procession honoring local service members and veterans. The station has been previewing the event, which draws crowds downtown each year. For a city with deep military ties, it's the centerpiece of the holiday calendar.

**According to Bakersfield Now, Bakersfield prepares for its Veterans Day parade**, with organizers and participants making final arrangements ahead of this morning's march. The coverage highlights the planning that goes into the event and the community groups taking part.

**Bakersfield Now also reports that homicides in the city have plunged since 2021**, a downward trend that marks real progress — but police caution that youth gun violence persists as a stubborn concern. The takeaway for residents is a mixed one: the long-term numbers are moving in the right direction, even as officers say the work with young people and firearms is far from finished.

**KGET 17 reports that a warrant has been issued after a man charged in a 2023 DUI injury case failed to appear in court.** The case stems from a crash that left someone injured, and the no-show now puts the defendant's status in front of a judge in a different way. It's a reminder that court dates carry consequences when they're missed.

**23ABC spoke with a U.S. Army veteran about the "wealth of information" now available on services for veterans.** The conversation focused on how much has changed in what's offered to those who served, and where veterans and their families can turn for help. On Veterans Day, it's a useful pointer to resources that many eligible residents may not know exist.

**23ABC reports that Pete Hegseth survived a second call for his impeachment**, after the House voted 211-204 on Tuesday to kill Kentucky Republican Congressman Thomas Massie's effort. Massie described his push as a gentler version of the investigations he expects Democrats to pursue when they take control of Congress in January, and argued Hegseth remains responsible for military actions carried out under President Trump's orders. The eight articles targeted Hegseth's role in operations involving Venezuela, Iran, Yemen, and the Caribbean; Hegseth said he stands behind every one of those operations. 23ABC talked with Kern County veterans, some of whom backed Hegseth as simply carrying out the president's direction, while others said they weren't fans of the dishonesty coming from the White House.

## Something good

The Giving Machine is coming back to Bakersfield for a second year, and that's worth a smile. The big red vending machine lets people buy essential goods and services for neighbors in need rather than for themselves. Five local nonprofits will benefit this year — CAPK Food Bank, Golden Empire Gleaners, The Salvation Army, Flood Ministries, and Catholic Charities of Bakersfield. Last year's machine raised roughly $80,000 for local groups, and organizers say 100 percent of donations go straight to the participating nonprofits. City lead Michelle Lord told 23ABC that Bakersfield was chosen because it's "such a caring community," and that the goal is simple: make the holidays meaningful for neighbors here at home. Organizers are also planning community performances and family activities around the machine's run.

## Coming up this week

The Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee meets Friday, November 13, at noon — a good one for anyone interested in cleanup efforts and neighborhood improvement around the city. Also on the calendar, the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meets Tuesday, November 17, at 2 p.m., and the Historic Preservation Commission meets that same day at 4 p.m.

Looking further out, the City Council holds two sessions on Wednesday, November 18 — a 3:30 p.m. meeting and a 5:15 p.m. meeting — so check the agendas if you want to weigh in on what's before the dais.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate ahead. NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet arrives Friday, November 13. The 20th Anniversary of the Bakersfield Country Music Awards takes the stage Sunday, November 15. Later in the month come Cults & Classics: Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? on November 23, Becky Robinson's Holiday Spectacular on November 27, and the Shrek Rave — Shrek The Halls — on December 4. And if you're already thinking about next year, season passes for Cults & Classics 2026-2027 are on sale now.

However you spend the holiday, take a moment to thank a veteran today — and enjoy the warm one we've got.
